Chapter 18 of 19

Far Shore

North Vancouver across Burrard Inlet
The story

Across Burrard Inlet, the lights of North Vancouver climb the lower slopes of the mountains. Seen from the south side of the water, on the right night, they seem to arrange themselves into flowing shapes, like a script written in a language nobody in Terminal City speaks.

The Far Shore is where things the city cannot understand get translated. Material from the Probes and from The Beyond arrives as noise; from here it comes back as patterns the Wire Choir can use. Nobody has ever read the lights out loud, and they never spell anything real. They only resolve into something usable, and only from the other side of the water.

The city is not sure the Far Shore has earned its place. It stays on probation, the weakest part of the whole system, kept for now because the image is beautiful and the job is real. Far shore. Light by light. Read the night. Send it back.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
